column1: To understand why, consider what would happen if expected inflation were to rise. Since (8.25) does not allow for any endogenous feedback from this rise in expected inflation to the nominal interest rate, the real interest rate must fall. This decline in the real interest rate is expansionary, and the output gap increases. The rise in output increases actual inflation, according to (8.20). Thus, a change in expected inflation, even if due to factors unrelated to the fundamentals of inflation, can set o¤ a self-fulfilling change in actual inflation.
